structured_output.hypothesis: If Darwin is right, native (non-introduced) frogs, toads and newts will be recorded on essentially none of a fixed list of truly oceanic islands (never joined to a continent), while introduced amphibians are recorded as established on some of those same islands.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Before looking at the data, fix a list of at least 15 oceanic islands or archipelagos that were volcanic and never connected to a continent. The list is: Hawaii, Galápagos, Azores, Madeira, Canary Islands, Cape Verde, St Helena, Ascension, Tristan da Cunha, Mauritius, Réunion, Society Islands, Marquesas, Cook Islands, Samoa, Tonga, Kerguelen and Bermuda. The claim passes if AmphibiaWeb lists native amphibians on at most 1 of these islands or archipelagos, which is 5% or less of the list. It must also record at least one introduced, established amphibian population on 3 or more of them, which tests the 'introduced frogs thrive' part.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim fails if native, non-introduced amphibian species are documented on 3 or more of the pre-listed oceanic islands or archipelagos, which is about 17% or more of the list. It also fails if no introduced amphibians are recorded as established on any of them, because that would remove the evidence that the islands are habitable. Two native-amphibian islands is an inconclusive result.
structured_output.interpretation: 'Batrachians' is read as modern Anura plus Caudata. Caecilians (Gymnophiona) are excluded because Darwin did not mention them. 'Oceanic islands' is read in the modern geological sense: islands that arose from the ocean floor and were never land-connected to a continent. Continental fragments such as New Zealand, Madagascar, the Seychelles, New Caledonia and Fiji are excluded in advance, and so are land-bridge islands such as Britain, Sri Lanka and Borneo. 'Naturally absent' is read as no native species in the country or island distribution fields. Introduced species are taken from the introduced-range or distribution notes in species accounts. The sea-water mechanism (that sea-water kills adults and spawn) is not tested directly. Only the distributional pattern and the habitability inference are tested. Species-level distribution text will be checked by hand against the island list.

dataset.name: AmphibiaWeb
dataset.why_it_fits: AmphibiaWeb is a global database of amphibian species. Its species accounts give country and island distribution, native or introduced status, and taxonomy (Anura and Caudata). Searching the distribution text or country fields for each pre-listed island or archipelago shows whether any native species is recorded and whether introduced populations are noted. The fields used are species name, order, distribution/range text, and introduced-status notes.
